Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://vvww.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 152 s. 2022 December 21 , 2022 ENGR. RAYMUND C. OLIVO, MPM, CESE Municipal Local Government Operation Officer Municipality of Matanao, Province of Davao del Sur Dear Engr. Olivo: This has reference to your letter dated 13 September 2022, which was elevated to the Central Office by DILG-Region Xl Director Alex C. Roldan, wherein you are seeking a legal opinion regarding the following issues: 1. Whether or not the Sangguniang Bayan has legislative authority to allow/authorize the conduct of traditional cockfighting in barangay, as part of the celebration of Araw ng Barangay upon the approval by the Chief of Police pursuant to Section 5 of Presidential Decree No. 449 (PD No. 449), in consonance with paragraph 4.1 of DILG Memorandum Circular 2022-003 dated 19 January 2022; and 2. If in the positive, could the traditional cockfighting be held in the barangay and not in the licensed cockpit? At the outset, we deem it proper to highlight Section 5 of presidential Decree No. 449 (PD 449), otherwise known as the Cockfighting Law of 1974, lays down the guidelines in holding of cockfights, to wit: Section 5. Cockpits and Cockfighting: In General: (d) Holding of Cockfights. Except as provided in this Decree, cockfighting shall be allowed only in licensed cockpits durinq Sundays and legal holida sanddurin local fiestas fornot more than threeda s. It ma also be held during provincial, city or municipal. agricultural. commercial or industrial fair. camival or exposition for a similar period of three days upon resolution ofthe province, city or municipality where such fair, carnival or exposition is to be held, subiect to the approval of the Chief of Constabulary or his authorized representative: Provided, that, no cockfighting on the occasion of such fair, camival or exposition shall be allowed within the month of a local fiesta or for more than two occasions a year in the same city or municipality: Provided, further, that "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

no cockfighting shall be held on December 30 (Rizal Day), June 12 (Philippine Independence Day) November 30 (National Heroes Day), Holy Thursday, Good Friday, Election or Referendum Day and during Registration Days for such election or referendum. (e) Cockfighting for Entertainment of Tourists or for Charitable Purposes. Subject to the preceding subsection hereof, the Chief Constabulary or his authorized representative may also allow the holdinq of cockfiqhting for the entertainment of foreiqn diqnitaries or for tourists. or for returning Filipinos. commonly known as "Balikbavan". or for the support of national fund-raising campaiqns for charitable purposes as mav be authorized bv the Office of the President: upon resolution of a provincial board. city or municipal council: in licensed cockpits or in plavqrounds or parks: Provided, that this privilege shall be extended for only one time, for a period not exceeding three days, within a year to a province, city, or municipality. It is clear from the afore-quoted provisions that cockfighting may only be held during Sundays: leqal Holidays, local fiestas for not more than three (3) days. It may also be held during provincial, city, municipal, agricultural, commercial, industrial fairs, carnivals, or expositions for a similar period of three days upon resolution of the province, city or municipality where such fair, carnival or exposition is to be held, subject to the approval of the Chief of the Philippine National Police or his authorized representative. In addition, the PNP Chief may also allow the holding of cockfighting for the entertainment of foreign dignitaries or for tourists, or for returning Filipinos, commonly known as "Balikbayan", or for the support of national fund-raising campaigns for charitable purposes as may be authorized by the Office of the President, upon resolution of a provincial board, city or municipal council, in licensed cockpits or in playgrounds or parks. In reply to the first issue, we are of the opinion that the celebration of the Araw ng Barangay does not fall under any of the enumerated events under PD No. 449. Hence, the conduct of traditional cockfighting cannot be allowed or authorized, unless the date of such occasion will fall on a Sunday, a legal holiday, or fiesta. Relatedly, as to the second issue, while it is true that cockfighting falling under Sec. (e) of PD No. 449, may be held in licensed cockpits or in playgrounds or parks, other than in a licensed cockpit, however, we would like to emphasize that this will only apply if the cockfighting is for entertainment of foreign dignitaries or for tourists, or for returning Filipinos, commonly known as "Balikbayan", or for the support of national fund-raising campaigns for charitable purposes.

This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have sufficiently guided you on the matter. Thank you.
